mutant.description: Two mutants, neither applied to a tracked file. (1) RB2-AC4: ran the criterion's own invocation against a directory holding only the licence (the state of this tree before the faces were copied in) -- the issuer had already exercised the same arm and recorded FACES: [] / NO-FACES-OR-NO-LICENCE. (2) THE SERVED-ARTIFACT CHECK: requested a face that does not exist, /fonts/lato-700.woff2, from the dev server, as a negative control on the 'HTTP 200 means it is served' inference.
mutant.expected: (1) the AC4 form reports no faces and flips to NO-FACES-OR-NO-LICENCE. (2) the absent face is distinguishable from a present one.
mutant.observed: (1) FACES: [] LICENCE: ['OFL.txt'] -> NO-FACES-OR-NO-LICENCE, so the amended criterion discriminates where its predecessor could not. (2) THE NEGATIVE CONTROL EXPOSED A TRAP: the absent face ALSO returned HTTP 200, because Vite's dev server falls back to index.html -- 826 bytes of text/html. Status code alone therefore proves nothing. The discriminating evidence used instead: content-type font/woff2, the wOF2 signature in the first four bytes, and the served bytes hashing identical to the shipped bytes (08c7108a..., 0f8199f7...). A third negative control, document.fonts.check('NoSuchFaceXYZ'), also returned true and that instrument was discarded rather than cited.

determinism.method: RB2-AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4 each run twice with no source change between. The woff2 conversion was ALSO run twice per face into separate paths and the outputs compared byte-for-byte and then table-by-table with fontTools, because a sha256 is recorded as identifying evidence and a non-reproducible build would make that claim misleading if left unstated.
determinism.observed: The four command criteria: identical output both times (rc=0; 0/CLEARED; 0,0/SELF-HOSTED; the same two faces, hashes and licence). THE CONVERSION IS NOT BYTE-DETERMINISTIC, stated rather than hidden: two conversions of the same .ttf differ. Resolved by table-level comparison -- of 17 tables, exactly one (head) differs, in head.modified (a save timestamp, one second apart) and its derived checkSumAdjustment; head.created and every glyph, metric, cmap and name table are byte-identical. So the FONT is reproducible and the CONTAINER BYTES are not: the recorded sha256s identify the bytes shipped and served (verified equal), not a re-derivable build. Noted in portal/public/fonts/README.md so a future re-derivation does not read as tampering.
